sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The report targets PIRLS 2011 Grade 4 students (sampled when the average age is at least 9.5 years; Grade 4 was sampled in Canada). The sampling design is a two-stage stratified cluster sample: schools are sampled first and intact classrooms from the target grade are sampled second, with replacement schools held in reserve. Exclusions permitted at the national level include school-level exclusions for geographically remote/small schools, radically different grade structures/curricula, or special-needs-only instruction, and student-level exclusions for functional/intellectual disabilities or non-native language speakers; combined exclusions are capped (school+student exclusions cannot exceed 5% of the national target population; very small-school exclusions cannot exceed 2%). In Canada, the report aggregates results across nine participating provinces, with three provinces at benchmarking level, four at oversampling level, and two at the Canadian level (reported collectively as Canada overall).

data.outcome_summary: This PIRLS 2011 Canadian results report describes Grade 4 reading literacy achievement and related contextual factors using PIRLS’s international assessment framework. PIRLS 2011 is administered every five years and uses a two-stage stratified cluster design (schools, then intact classrooms), with permitted school- and student-level exclusions and caps to maintain comparability. The assessment includes multiple-choice and constructed-response items across two reading purposes (literary experience; acquire and use information) and four comprehension processes, with results reported on a 0–1000 PIRLS scale centered at 500 and benchmark categories (Advanced, High, Intermediate, Low). For Canada, the report reports achievement means, benchmark attainment percentages, and descriptive differences by language of instruction, sex, and several home, student, teacher, and school questionnaire scales. It emphasizes sampling error and measurement error via standard errors and confidence intervals, but the provided text does not specify PV estimation or missing-data procedures for any model-based analysis.
